liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Jam** (2 reviews): A nice jam follows the drums; The jam before drums, cut from the reviewer's old cassettes, is complete here and sustains energy into drums [11][18]
- **Space** (2 reviews): The drums-into-space transition is a favorite early-'80s mix-up jam, with spooky wind-like sounds; Around nine minutes into space, the band plays in eleven for about a minute, with strong Jerry accents [18][20]
- **Bertha** (1 review): Bertha takes about a verse before the band settles into its groove [13]
- **Candyman** (1 review): Jerry's vocal phrasing on Candyman is praised, making it a powerful version [13]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): The Scarlet into Fire pairing is called extremely hot, with high energy and spirits [16]
- **Fire on the Mountain** (1 review): This Fire is fun and solid, but lacks the yearning or mystery of the reviewer's favorites [19]
- **Saint of Circumstance** (1 review): Reviewer loves the jam coming out of Saint of Circumstance [11]

## Setlist highlights

- **Other One/Eleven Jam**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]

## The recordings

- **gd1982-08-06.mtx.seamons.ht58.125889.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 25 songs; 184 min; rated 4.17/5 by 6 [1]
- **gd82-08-06.sonyecm.norman.7288.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 24 songs; 185 min; rated 4.77/5 by 13 [4]. Said about its sound: Audience recording is slightly boomy but puts you around fifteen rows back, dead center, with nice instrumental balance; Sound quality is very good, though the reviewer would turn Phil up a bit [9][16]
- **gd1982-08-06.176350.aud.bernstein.ackerman.noel.flac2496**: audience recording; 23 songs; 191 min [5]. Said about its sound: Bernstein's recording sounds upfront and centered on a quick listen [5]
- **gd82-08-06.sbd.fink.15028.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 18 songs; 173 min; rated 4.2/5 by 5 [8]. Said about its sound: Soundboard sounds crystal clear [19]

## Around the show

- The show took place on a sweltering night in St. Paul [9]
- At the end, Bobby relays a request for someone in the crowd to get to first aid [13]
- Reviewer says early-eighties soundboards tend to lose Lesh, while this audience tape keeps him audible [9]
- Sounds more frantic than the Starlight show, as if played for a hyped-up crowd [11]
- Reviewer calls it a hidden gem among 1982 shows, another strong Minnesota performance despite looking plain on paper [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1982-08-06.mtx.seamons.ht58.125889.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix by Hunter Seamons using Final Cut Pro (SHN & FLAC > AIFF > Final Cut w/EQ > AIFF CD tracking via Audacity > FLAC16 via xACT w/meta-tagging and embedded… [1]. Also: Credits: OHR Weinberg recorded; Charlie Miller transferred the soundboard; Jim Wise and Todd Norman transferred the audience source [1]
- **gd82-08-06.sonyecm.norman.7288.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Jim Wise; source: Audience Recording: Sony ECM 23-F's [4]
- **gd1982-08-06.176350.aud.bernstein.ackerman.noel.flac2496**: taped by Jon Bernstein; transferred by Transfer & Mastering by Ray Ackerman Edited & Processed w/ add'l Mastering by Joe Noel January 25, 2026; source: ?? mics > ?? lead deck > Sony TC-D5 > Master Cassettes (Maxell XLIIS-90's) [5]. Also: Jon Bernstein recorded, Ray Ackerman made the transfer, and Ohr Weinberg supplied the patch source; Microphones and lead deck are not recalled; possibly Nak 300s [5]
- **gd82-08-06.sbd.fink.15028.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [8]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1982-08-06 Backstage Pass - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1982-08-06-backstage-pass/) [22]
